c.st: CEO fired developers to make room for AI. Developers create open source AI CEO
c.x:
>qIf you have the right underlings (or inherit them) you might actually not need to do anything at all and succeed. Then again if you have the wrong underlings (or inherit them) then your job is hella-difficult.”

I think this paragraph is right on the money, but the ‘leader’ has more influence on their ‘underlings’ than you give them credit for. In this vein, I highly recommend “Turn the Ship Around!” by Marquet, which is the only good book on leadership I’ve managed to find.

c.st: Ask for no, don't ask for yes (2022)
c.x: This works great from a leadership perspective as well. If anyone is interested, I can recommend the book Turn the Ship Around! by David Marquet about this very subject.

c.st: Ask for no, don't ask for yes (2022)
c.x:
I've used this technique ever since I read DHH's article about the book "Turn The Ship Around" [1].  The book's author, a Naval officer, had a policy of "Don't come to me for permission, come to me with intent."  Hearing that phrase changed my professional life for the better in so many ways.

Admittedly I haven't included a deadline nearly as often, but I've found a huge difference between saying "Can I do XYZ?" to my team lead (or even worse, "What should I do?"), vs. "Unless you object, I plan to do XYZ."  The…

c.st: Valve's flat structure contains “hidden layer of powerful management”
c.x:
related to company structure, I recently read "Turn the ship around!" and found it to be a great book on leadership (its Harvard business school meets the red october, if you're not familiar)

Anyone have any experience with Leader-Leader at a company? I feel like it would mostly work, but there are some variables I think that might need attention.

I used to be a big admirer of Matt and Automattic, but after this whole WP Engine episode I've lost respect. I shut down my old wordpress blog, still working on importing the posts as org-mode files onto my new site, I no longer recommend WP to non-techies that ask me how to build a website.

I hope WordPress (and Automattic) turn the ship around but its not looking good at this point.

c.st: Microsoft raises Xbox prices by up to 43%
c.x:
I really don't get what MS is doing here. They claim they care about Xbox, that they're going to turn the ship around, yet they cluelessly and carelessly laid off most of their best staff, all while raising prices multiple times and still not producing a coherent future roadmap.

Any consumer or customer would look at this behavior pattern and think they are far too unstable to put their trust into.

At this point it's time to call it for Xbox. I don't think they'll be around in six months time.
